correctness.rationale: Gaussian orthogonal decomposition yields independent chi-square(k) and chi-square(s-k+1) and expected excess k/(s-k-1), diverging for s<=k+1 unless exact residual zero. Chebyshev extremizer weights w_i proportional to 1/(lambda_i |prod_{j!=i}(lambda_i-lambda_j)|) satisfy all GMRES normal equations via barycentric identities. Discrete ratio e^{2a}t/(t+1) selects the asymptotic reserve; comparison bound confines all finite-s minimizers to a fixed finite reserve set, and the exact B_K integer tie is broken by the finite denominator. Independent high-precision tests resolved the numerical near-tie: B_K=1 exactly for K=17+12sqrt(2), and at s=20,100,180 the larger reserve 2 wins. A double-precision test at s=100 initially misclassified this tie; this was diagnosed as precision loss, not a mathematical counterexample.
